body:
`.gitignore:251` reads `frontend/node_modules/`. The trailing slash restricts the
rule to **directories**, so a `node_modules` that is a **symlink** is not ignored
— git sees a file, `git check-ignore` reports no match, and it shows up as an
untracked path that `git add -A` will happily commit.

What lands if it does: a symlink whose target is an absolute path on one
machine. It breaks for every other contributor and in CI, and it reads as noise
in review rather than as a bug.

Observed 2026-08-10 while building the zero-egress report builder: a worktree on
the Crucial X8 had no `node_modules`, so it was symlinked to the main checkout's
copy to run `tsc`/`vite` without a second 167 MB install. `git status` then
listed `frontend/node_modules` as untracked, and `git check-ignore -v` confirmed
no rule matched. Only staging files explicitly avoided committing it.

Symlinking `node_modules` is not exotic — pnpm does it by default, and it is the
obvious move for a throwaway worktree.

Fix: drop the trailing slash (`frontend/node_modules`), which matches both a
directory and a symlink. Worth a sweep of `.gitignore` for sibling
directory-only rules covering paths that are commonly symlinked.
title: gitignore's trailing-slash node_modules rule does not match a symlinked node_modules
